title: AC Dey Drink Fuel?

lines.text: Oga driver, abeg on the AC! This Lagos sun dey fry me like plantain!
AC?! Ahn ahn, madam! You wan finish my fuel? This AC dey drink fuel pass generator!
Generator? Oga, na small car you dey drive, no be I-better-pass-my-neighbour!
AC dey spoil engine! Open window. Na natural AC, free of charge!
My pikin. Come, make I show you something.
Same belt dey turn your alternator and your AC compressor. AC off? E dey spin free. AC on? Small load. Like one extra passenger.
So yes, AC dey use fuel. But small! Five to ten percent. For go-slow, maybe four to seven hundred naira per hour. No be tanker!
And that your open window for expressway? The breeze dey drag your motor back. Fuel still dey go!
But Baba... fuel don reach thirteen hundred naira o!
Oga, no wahala. I go just rate you when I land.
Ahn ahn! Madam, wait! See as e cold now! AC na investment!
AC no be your problem. Fuel go finish anyhow, na five stars dey refill tank. On the AC!

facts_note: AC typically adds ~5-10% fuel use in normal driving (more in heavy heat/stop-go) and ~0.3-0.5 L/hour extra when idling. At ~N1,369/L (NNPC Lagos, late Oct 2026) that is roughly N400-N700 per hour of go-slow. Estimates; varies by car, AC condition and weather.
